coalition_name: Hawaii State Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person commits harassment by stalking by engaging in a course of conduct involving pursuit, surveillance, or nonconsensual contact on more than one occasion without legitimate purpose, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm or in reckless disregard of that risk.
criminal_penalty: Misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and a fine up to $2,000; a repeat offense within 5 years is aggravated harassment by stalking under HRS 711-1106.4, a Class C felony.
cyber_note: Hawaii has no separate cyberstalking statute; nonconsensual contact under HRS 711-1106.5 expressly includes contact by telephone, facsimile, or any form of electronic communication, including email.
order_duration: A temporary restraining order lasts up to 90 days; a final injunction lasts up to 3 years.
order_free_note: There is a $15 filing fee, which can be waived in exceptional circumstances.
order_name: Injunction Against Harassment (with Temporary Restraining Order)
order_where: File a written petition in the District Court of the district where you live, where the respondent lives, or where the harassment occurred.

coalition_name: Idaho Coalition Against Sexual & Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Knowingly and maliciously engaging in a course of conduct of repeated nonconsensual contact that would cause a reasonable person substantial emotional distress or fear of death or injury to that person or a family or household member.
criminal_penalty: Second-degree stalking is a misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and a $1,000 fine; first-degree stalking is a felony, 1 to 5 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000.
cyber_note: Covers using telecommunication, email, text, or other electronic communication with intent to annoy, terrify, threaten, intimidate, harass, or offend, including repeated communications that disturb the peace.
order_duration: Up to 1 year, renewable on motion for good cause.
order_where: File a verified petition with the magistrate division of the district court in the county where the respondent lives, where you live, or where you are temporarily residing.

criminal_definition: Knowingly engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person, knowing or having reason to know it would cause a reasonable person to fear for safety or suffer emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Class 4 felony, 1 to 3 years in prison; a second or subsequent conviction is a Class 3 felony, 2 to 5 years in prison.
cyber_note: Covers harassing another person through electronic communication on at least two occasions, including transmitting threats or creating a harassing website or webpage.
order_duration: An emergency order lasts 14 to 21 days; a plenary order lasts up to 2 years and can be extended.
order_free_note: No fee is charged by the clerk for filing petitions or modifying or certifying orders, and the sheriff serves the papers at no cost to the petitioner (740 ILCS 21/20).
order_where: File a petition in any Illinois circuit court, including the county where either party lives or where the stalking occurred.

criminal_definition: Knowingly or intentionally engaging in a course of conduct involving repeated or continuing harassment that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or threatened, and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: Level 6 felony, 6 months to 2 1/2 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000; a Level 5 felony, 1 to 6 years in prison, if aggravating factors apply.
cyber_note: Indiana has no separate cyberstalking statute; its harassment law covers using a computer network or other electronic communication to communicate with a person or send obscene or profane messages, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm and no intent of legitimate communication.
order_duration: Normally 2 years, unless the judge sets a different date.
order_free_note: No fees are charged for filing, service of process, witness fees, or subpoena fees in a protection-order case.
order_where: File a petition with the clerk of the court in your county; Indiana also offers online filing through the state Protection Order Registry.

criminal_definition: Purposefully engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or threatened, or to fear bodily injury or death to that person or an immediate family member.
criminal_penalty: A first offense is an aggravated misdemeanor; a second offense is a Class D felony; a Class C felony if committed while subject to a protective order, while using a technological device, or under other aggravating circumstances.
cyber_note: Iowa has no separate cyberstalking statute; stalking under section 708.11 includes repeatedly using a technological device to locate, listen to, or watch a person without authorization or legitimate purpose, which elevates the offense to a Class C felony.
order_duration: A Chapter 236 protective order lasts for a fixed period of up to 1 year, with unlimited extensions if the defendant still poses a threat.
order_free_note: The filing fee and court costs for a Chapter 236 order for protection are waived for the plaintiff, and service is performed without charge to the plaintiff.
order_gap_note: Iowa has no standalone civil stalking order — a stalking victim uses a Chapter 236 Domestic Abuse Protective Order only if the stalker is a family/household member; otherwise protection comes through a criminal No Contact Order under Chapter 664A, issued by the court in a criminal case (not filed by the victim).
order_name: Domestic Abuse Protective Order; criminal No Contact Order
order_where: File a verified petition for a Chapter 236 protective order in the district court of the county where either party lives; a Chapter 664A no-contact order is issued by the court in a criminal case and is not filed by the victim.

coalition_name: Kansas Coalition Against Sexual and Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Recklessly or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct targeted at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for the safety of that person or an immediate family member, and that actually places the targeted person in such fear.
criminal_penalty: A first offense under subsection (a)(1) is a Class A person misdemeanor; a second or subsequent conviction is a severity level 7 person felony, with higher felony levels for protective-order violations and other aggravating circumstances.
cyber_note: Kansas has no separate cyberstalking statute; the stalking statute covers a course of conduct including use of an electronic tracking system to determine the targeted person's location, movement, or travel patterns.
order_duration: A final order lasts for a fixed period of not less than 1 year and not more than 2 years, extendable for 1 to 3 more years, or up to the defendant's lifetime if the order was violated or other statutory conditions are met.
order_free_note: No docket fee is charged for filing a petition under K.S.A. 60-31a04.
order_name: Protection from Stalking, Sexual Assault, or Human Trafficking Order
order_where: File a petition in any Kansas district court.

coalition_name: ZeroV (formerly Kentucky Coalition Against Domestic Violence)
criminal_definition: Intentionally engaging in a course of conduct directed at another person that seriously alarms, annoys, intimidates, or harasses that person, serves no legitimate purpose, and causes substantial mental distress, while consciously disregarding a substantial and unjustifiable risk of causing that distress.
criminal_penalty: Stalking is a Class D felony, 1 to 5 years in prison; it is a Class C felony if a protective order was in effect, a criminal complaint was pending, there was a prior conviction against the same victim within 5 years, a deadly weapon was used, or the acts placed the victim in reasonable fear of sexual contact, physical injury, or death.
cyber_note: Kentucky has no separate cyberstalking statute; the course of conduct in KRS 508.130 expressly includes conduct by computer, the internet, social media, email, text, and other electronic means.
order_duration: A final interpersonal protective order lasts for a period fixed by the court, up to 3 years, and may be reissued for further periods of up to 3 years each.
order_free_note: No filing fee is charged to petition for a protective order in Kentucky.
order_where: File a petition with the Office of Circuit Court Clerk in the county where you live or the county you fled to for safety, for hearing in Circuit (Family) Court.

criminal_definition: Intentionally and repeatedly following or harassing another person in a way that would cause a reasonable person to feel alarmed or to suffer emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First conviction: a fine of $500 to $1,000 and 30 days to 1 year in jail; penalties increase for later convictions, victims under 18, use of a dangerous weapon, and protective-order violations.
cyber_note: Covers using electronic communication to threaten physical harm or extort, and repeatedly emailing or electronically communicating to threaten, terrify, or harass a person.
order_duration: A final protective order lasts for a fixed period of up to 18 months, extendable after a hearing; the portion ordering the defendant not to abuse, harass, or interfere with the victim may be made indefinite.
order_free_note: Louisiana law prohibits charging a victim for filing, issuing, or serving a protective order for domestic abuse, dating violence, stalking, or sexual assault.
order_name: Order of Protection under the Protection from Stalking Act
order_where: File a petition in any Louisiana district court empowered to hear civil matters, in the parish where you live.

coalition_name: Maine Coalition to End Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Intentionally or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to suffer serious inconvenience or emotional distress, or to fear bodily injury or death to that person, a close relation, or a pet.
criminal_penalty: Stalking is a Class D crime, up to 364 days in jail and a fine up to $2,000; it is a Class C crime, up to 5 years in prison and a $5,000 fine, for repeat offenders and other aggravating circumstances.
cyber_note: Maine has no separate cyberstalking statute; the course of conduct in 17-A M.R.S. § 210-A includes following, monitoring, tracking, observing, surveilling, threatening, or communicating with a person by any action, method, device, or means, including online.
order_duration: An initial final Protection from Harassment order lasts up to 1 year and may be extended.
order_free_note: There is no filing fee if the complaint is related to stalking, domestic violence, sexual assault, sex trafficking, or unlawful dissemination of private images; other harassment complaints may carry a fee.
order_where: File a complaint in the District Court of the division where you or the defendant lives.

criminal_definition: Engaging in a malicious course of conduct that includes approaching or pursuing another person, with intent to place that person in reasonable fear of serious bodily injury, assault, rape or a sexual offense, false imprisonment, or death, or knowing or reasonably knowing the conduct would cause such fear.
criminal_penalty: Stalking is a misdemeanor, up to 5 years in prison and a fine up to $5,000.
cyber_note: Covers maliciously engaging in a course of conduct through electronic communication that alarms or seriously annoys another, with intent to harass, alarm, or annoy, after a warning to stop and without legal purpose.
order_duration: A final peace order lasts for the period stated in the order, up to 6 months, and may be extended for up to another 6 months after a hearing for good cause.
order_free_note: There is a $46 filing fee and a $40 service fee; the court may waive the filing fee for indigent petitioners but cannot waive the service fee.
order_where: File a petition in the District Court of Maryland in the county where you live; if the court is closed, a District Court commissioner can issue an interim order.
